children: Australian shares fell to a one-month low on Wednesday, dragged down by miners and gold stocks, while surging oil prices fuelled inflation concerns and expectations of rate hikes ahead of a key economic output print due later in the day.
The S&P/ASX 200 index
was down 1.3% at 8,952.30 points, as at 0039 GMT, and on track for its weakest session since early-July, if current momentum persists. The benchmark closed 0.1% lower on Tuesday.
Concerns over a potential oil supply disruption took centerstage after the conflict between the U.S. and Iran resumed, reigniting inflation worries and pushing oil prices higher.

That bolstered the case for a rate hike by the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA), with markets pricing in a 50% chance that the central bank will add 25 basis points to the key rate as early as this month's meeting.
Investors will closely watch second-quarter GDP data due at 0130 GMT for clues on the RBA's interest rate trajectory ahead of its policy meeting.
Financials
and real estate (.AXRE) stocks fell 0.5% and 0.7%, respectively, while the "Big Four" banks lost between 0.3% and 0.9%.
The mining sub-index
fell as much as 3.5% to its lowest level in nearly a fortnight, with miners BHP Group
, Rio Tinto
and Fortescue
down between 2% and 3.4%.
Gold stocks
slumped as much as nearly 5%, hitting their lowest level in roughly two weeks as tepid gold prices weighed on the sector.
Shares of Northern Star Resources
and Evolution Mining fell 5.2% and 5%, respectively.
Energy stocks
rose as much as 1.8% and were set for their best session in a week as strong crude oil prices boosted the sector. Santos
and Woodside Energy
rose as much as 2.1% and 2.9%, respectively.
New Zealand's benchmark S&P/NZX 50 index
fell 0.6% to 13,705.63 points, as investors braced for the central bank's rate decision due at 0200 GMT.
Markets are pricing a quarter-basis-point hike to 2.75% in the key cash rate.
